rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act (good cause eviction protections)
rules.requirement: A residential landlord cannot evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease without good cause, as defined in state law. The landlord must serve a Notice to Quit and obtain a Judgment for Possession through the courts before the tenant can be removed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies in New Jersey (written or oral leases).
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to 
prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-cause (redevelopment/condemnation) evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts a tenant to permanently take the property off the rental market for redevelopment or to clear a blighted area, the landlord must serve at least three months' notice and provide relocation assistance before the tenant can be evicted.
rules.key_value: 6 times monthly rent (for illegal occupancy cause); relocation assistance required before eviction for redevelopment cause
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants evicted under the redevelopment/blight-clearance ground or illegal occupancy ground under the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.penalty: Landlord must repay municipality if tenant draws from revolving relocation fund; 18% annual interest accrues on unpaid relocation amounts owed to municipality if not paid timely.
rules.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit 
for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Foreclosure eviction notice protections
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord (or new owner) must provide a 90-day notice to quit when the property was purchased by a buyer intending to personally occupy it as a primary residence, and new owners must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days of sale that tenants are not required to move.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenants in foreclosed properties; month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are not exempt from the 90-day notice requirement.
rules.quoted_span:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.
